messages:
maya: heads-up — i'm iterating on the internal incident comms templates (status page + customer msgs + oncall handoff). want to lock tone and placeholders before we push to the playbook.

devlin: good call. main goals: 1) clarity for customers, 2) concise actionable notes for oncall, 3) single source of truth for followups. keep language simple.

sophia: agree. also want a small module for 'customer impact triage' so support can quickly classify.

jack: can we include an explicit 'what we know / what we're doing / next update ETA / how to contact' section? that's what PMs keep asking for.

maya: yes — leaning towards this structure for every external update:

- summary (1 sentence)
- scope + affected customers
- current status (investigating/mitigating/resolved)
- customer impact (user-visible symptoms)
- mitigation/next steps (what team is doing)
- ETA for next update or resolution if known
- contact / workaround / escalation link

devlin: +1. also propose tone variants:
- "technical": short, precise, include logs/metrics link.
- "customer-friendly": non-technical, focus on impact and mitigation.
- "regulatory/enterprise": formal + link to post-incident review and audit contact.

maya: dropping a draft block for the status page (customer-friendly) — please react with :thumbsup: / :eyes: / suggestions inline.

```
[Status page]
Summary: We are experiencing increased latency for inference requests in the us-west-2 region.
Scope: A subset of hosted API requests using model-x by customers in us-west-2.
Status: Investigating.
Customer impact: Higher than normal response times (1.2–3s additional latency). No data loss.
Mitigation: Engineers are rolling a partial rollback to the previous runtime and monitoring error rates.
Next update: in 20 minutes or sooner if we have a status change.
Workaround: Retry requests or route to us-east-1 for lower latency.
Contact: support@redwood.ai or incident channel #incidents.
```

maya: internal notification template (for cross-team comms):

```
[Internal]
Root cause (initial): under investigation — suspected kernel regression after runtime deploy.
Impact: increased tail latency for model-x in us-west-2 affecting ~12% of requests.
Actions in-flight: rollback to previous runtime, enable extra logging, throttle non-critical background jobs.
On-call: @devlin (primary), @jack (secondary).
Next handoff: 2026-10-20 03:45 UTC - handoff notes will be posted to this thread.
Required escalation: if latency > 1s above baseline for >30m, page infra-sre and product-ops.
Postmortem owners: eng-runtime + eng-sre.
```

devlin: i like the escalation thresholds. suggestion: add a single-line 'customer messaging owner' so support knows who sends public updates.

sophia: +1 — also include a small checklist for the person doing the oncall handoff: last action taken, open tasks, expected next actions, any temporary mitigations. Example:

```
Oncall handoff checklist:
- last action: rolled back runtime v7.2 -> v7.1
- open tasks: validate traffic routing, confirm error rates drop to baseline
- mitigations in place: extra logging, rate-limiter applied to batch jobs
- known unknowns: single shard still showing elevated p95 latency
```

jack: can we standardize placeholders so automation can populate them? like {region}, {affected_pct}, {root_cause_tentative}, {eta_next_update}.

maya: yes — i'll make a canonical placeholder list and add it to the template header.

incident-bot: automatic note — incident thread created by @maya at 1790012345. Please append live updates using this thread.

devlin: one more thing — tone guidance for customer emails: avoid definitive blame in early updates ("we are investigating" not "we caused"), be empathetic, and provide clear workaround if possible. short subject line: "Service disruption affecting inference latency — us-west-2".

maya: adding three short subject templates:
- Customer (urgent): "Service disruption affecting inference latency — {region}"
- Customer (informational): "Intermittent latency observed — {region}, update"
- Enterprise/regulatory: "Incident report: {incident_id} — {short_summary}"

sophia: for enterprise templates, include a 'data exposure' checkbox. default: "no evidence of data exposure" if true, otherwise escalate to security-comms.

maya: pasting a compact customer email example (friendly, minimal):

```
Subject: Service disruption affecting inference latency — us-west-2

Hi —
We’re currently investigating increased response times for inference requests in our us-west-2 region which may affect some requests. Our engineers are rolling back a recent runtime change and monitoring results. There’s no evidence of data loss.

What we’re doing: rollback in progress; monitoring error/latency metrics.
Workaround: route traffic to us-east-1 or retry requests.
Next update: in ~20 minutes.
If you need immediate assistance, reply to this email or contact support@redwood.ai.

Thanks for your patience,
The Redwood Inference team
```

maya: also placing a 'post-incident followup' skeleton we want included in every postmortem email to customers who were affected:

- Timeline of events (concise)
- Root cause (final)
- Customer impact (specific accounts/regions if required)
- Mitigations implemented
- Preventative actions + ETA for completion
- Point of contact for questions

jack: tiny nit — include a single sentence at the top for executive readers, e.g., "Impact was limited to a subset of customers in us-west-2; no data loss."

devlin: i can make a tiny python script to render templates from placeholders and post to statuspage via API. will add in infra docs.

maya: excellent. plan: i'll update the playbook with these templates and a short 'how to pick a tone' flowchart. intend to ship by EOD. please add inline comments here if you want wording changes.

oncall-handoff-bot: handoff reminder set — next scheduled handoff at 1790012700 UTC.

sophia: quick suggestion about language: avoid absolute timelines unless we mean them. use 'approximately' or 'expected' when uncertain.

maya: agreed — i'll mark ETA fields as 'approx.' unless we have confident estimates.

jack: :thumbsup: nice work. this will make post-incident comms way smoother.

maya: thanks — closing loop after i push the PR. will ping again for final sign-off.

incident-bot: auto-update — template PR created by @maya: https://git.internal/redwood/comms-templates/pulls/42
